top.description: Cedar Ridge wide receiver Carter Copeland (12) advances the ball as Rouse safety Liam Mongold (13) defends as Cedar Ridge football takes on Rouse at Cedar Ridge in Austin on Friday, Sept. 18, 2026. (Mikala Compton/Austin American-Statesman) As Ike Riemenschneider stood near midfield before the coin toss of Rouse's Oct. 22 clash against Hutto, an official took him by surprise. "All the referees know you, they always talk about you," the 6-foot-6, 270-pound senior was told. "They always talk about you, like ‘Have you seen that guy from Rouse? He's huge.'" Riemenschneider doesn't just stand out because of his stature. He's also somewhat of an anomaly within high school football. Riemenschneider converted from tight end to offensive line this season, and now serves as the left tackle for an offense averaging 31.6 points per game. What is unique is that he also handles punter and kicker duties for the Raiders, a role that is stereotypically held by a slender specialist or skill position player. MORE: High school football rankings Riemenschneider, who dubs himself the "Biggest Kicker in Texas" on social media - a fact the Statesman could not verify with certainty - has thrived this fall on the line and with his booming boot. Both aspects of his game will be crucial again Thursday as Rouse (4-5, 2-3) aims to claim the final playoff spot in District 24-6A in a must-win game against East View (4-5, 2-3). "Every week he's getting better," Rouse head coach Mark Hopkins said of Riemenschneider's performance as the team's blindside blocker. "He's grown not just into a guy that's out there trying to figure out what to do, but telling other guys and making sure the calls are right and understanding the big picture of things. So he's doing a really good job." Rouse offensive lineman Ike Riemenschneider (76) kicks a field goal as Cedar Ridge football takes on Rouse at Cedar Ridge in Austin on Friday, Sept. 18, 2026. (Mikala Compton/Austin American-Statesman) An injury leads to a new passion Before Riemenschneider put on pads and a helmet, he was a soccer-loving kid who idolized Swedish striker Zlatan Ibrahimović, an uber-confident star who suited up for many of the sport's European giants, such as FC Barcelona, Paris Saint Germain and Manchester United. But as Riemenschneider grew into a larger frame in middle school, football coaches took notice and swayed him to try the sport. In seventh grade, he ended up breaking his arm, limiting his chances to get on the field. "To combat that, I started to learn how to punt and kick, and it's just stuck ever since," he said. "I really like it, and I'm pretty decent at it." top.title: How the Rockets lost their second game of the season: they couldn't stop LaMelo Ball in final quarter
top.description: Houston Rockets players Fred Vanvleet (5), Kevin Durant (7), Alperen Sengun (28) and Tari Eason (17) talk after a timeout at the Toyota Center in Houston on Wednesday, Nov. 4, 2026. Houston Rockets fell to the Minnesota Timberwolves 117-107. (Elizabeth Conley/Houston Chronicle) Down the final stretch of Wednesday night's matchup with the Minnesota Timberwolves, Houston Rockets coach Ime Udoka toggled between a few different lineups. Udoka played his usual starting five - Fred VanVleet, Amen Thompson, Jabari Smith Jr., Kevin Durant and Alperen Şengün - for a little more than two minutes. He went to a small-ball variation with Tari Eason in Şengün's place for about 90 seconds, then put Sengun back in for Smith to close out the final 2:10, according to FadeAway's lineup data. What led to the changes? "Trying to get a stop," Udoka said. ROCKETS MAILBAG: Can Amen Thompson touch the top of the backboard? Houston couldn't get enough stops, giving up 35 points in a fourth quarter it lost by 12 en route to its second defeat of the season, 117-107, at Toyota Center. The Timberwolves, playing without star Anthony Edwards, got a strong late-game showing from point guard LaMelo Ball. Udoka said the Rockets did a good job guarding Ball for about three and a half quarters, and he was right. Ball scored 12 of his 20 points and had two of his six assists in the final seven minutes. "I just think we were too loose on them the whole game and they got going," said Durant, who led Houston with 21 points but was one of three Rockets - along with Şengün and VanVleet - with four turnovers. Giveaways were a major problem Wednesday, with 22 Houston miscues leading to 33 Minnesota points. Udoka said the Rockets had poor awareness when kicking the ball out after touching the paint against a Timberwolves defense that routinely sent help. "I lead by example out there, so I can't be leading the team in turnovers," Durant said. Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. top.title: Three of the biggest threats to a Notre Dame victory over Miami
top.description: SOUTH BEND, INDIANA - OCTOBER 10: CJ Carr #13 of the Notre Dame Fighting Irish runs the ball against the Stanford Cardinal at Notre Dame Stadium on October 10, 2026 in South Bend, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images Saturday is rapidly approaching and we are all eager to see how Notre Dame responds to the recent challenge laid before them by the college football playoff committee — beat Miami or plan on watching the playoffs from home. But what obstacles lay in Notre Dame’s way? What are some of the biggest threats to that victory? MISCOMMUNICATION Despite the loss of wide receiver Malachi Toney, Miami still has a potent offense, and the Irish need to play much better on defense than they did against BYU. One of the big issues in that loss was the lack of communication or just plain miscommunication on defense. Assignments were blown, and the Irish looked lost at times. We saw similar things in losses to Miami and Texas A&M last year. If Notre Dame can’t play with more discipline and poise, they could suffer the same fate. THE SLOW START In most pf the games Notre Dame has lost during the Marcus Freeman era, we see that the team tends to come out flat — and more than that even. They’re flat, timid, confused, and even overzealous. They work themselves into a hole, and then spend two or more quarters trying to overcome its beginning nonsense. If the Irish can come out swinging and kind of “catch that groove” early, things should work in their favor, but if not… it will be a much MUCH heavier load (especially with the weight of the stakes of this game). COWARDLY PLAY Don’t do it. Do NOT get regrettably conservative. CJ Carr has that issue during most games, and it’s like he’s too afraid to make a mistake — so he overthrows a guy here and then under throws a guy there. He doesn’t turn the ball over , and that’s definitely important, but in a game like this — he needs to unleash himself. That can be accomplished by Freeman having a conversation with him and Mike Denbrock. In that same conversation, Freeman can remind both that Carr has legs, and despite not using them much this season — maybe Saturday would be a good time to use them a bit more. Don’t be cowards — do something different.

top.title: The Panthers Should Add This Versatile Lineman in the Draft
top.description: COLUMBIA, MISSOURI - OCTOBER 03: Cayden Green #70 of the Missouri Tigers blocks Jeramiah McCloud #91 of the Florida Gators at Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium on October 03, 2026 in Columbia, Missouri. (Photo by Jay Biggerstaff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2027 NFL Draft feels like forever away, and we’re all caught up in the start of the NFL season. Regardless, it’s never too early to look ahead to the Draft. This weekly series will take a closer look at some of the prospects the Carolina Panthers could select in the 2027 iteration of the Draft. In this series, we’ll only be looking at prospects the Panthers could seriously consider. Today our profile will focus on Missouri Tigers offensive lineman Cayden Green. Bio Green (6’5”, 325 lbs.) was a four star recruit and ranked as the state of Missouri’s second best prospect coming out of high school in 2022. Originally signing with Oklahoma, he started five games for the Sooners at left guard before transferring back to his home state. Green continued to hold down the left guard spot until 2025, when the Tigers moved him to left tackle. In his first year at the position, he allowed only seven pressures across over 350 pass blocking snaps, earning him First Team All-SEC recognition. After missing the first game due to injury, Green has been a stalwart at left tackle for the Tigers, allowing five pressures and zero sacks through five games this year. Strengths/Weaknesses One of Green’s biggest strengths is how naturally he took to the change of position. Usually linemen make the transition outside in, but in his first season moving from guard to tackle he earned All-SEC honors. On top of that, the switch to left tackle happened just two weeks before the 2025 season, showing just how coachable and adaptable he is. Green uses his heavy frame to anchor well and has the athleticism to not get beat around the edge on speed rushes. He is a coach’s dream: finishing blocks and playing through the whistle with a true versatility that will total over 1,500 snaps at guard and tackle in his career. While performing well, Green is still new to the left tackle position. His performance this year has really solidified his ranking among the Draft’s top tackles, but there are still some raw moments. He has also battled injuries the last couple of seasons. Nothing major, but still something that some teams might want to look further into. Projection Green is the epitome of a player that every coaching staff wants. He has the coachability and versatility to immediately start at a minimum of three positions on the offensive line, he is consistent in his performance against SEC competition, and he does not commit penalties (flagged just twice so far this season). As he continues to grow into the position, expect his stock to continue rising through the middle of the first round, potentially higher after teams get to interview him at the Combine. top.title: Orioles news: Rotation needs, possible solutions
top.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 15: Shane Baz #34 of the Baltimore Orioles in action during the game against the New York Mets at Citi Field on September 15, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Evan Bernstein/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello, friends. There are now 139 days remaining until the next scheduled Orioles game. Everyone has their own different level of pessimism for how likely it is that MLB’s owner-imposed lockout of the players will end by then in order to allow the season to begin. How you feel about the Orioles rotation minus Trevor Rogers probably has a lot to do with how much urgency you think the team should have this offseason. The team had a “could have been worse” rotation in 2026 even with Rogers being as good as he was from about June on to the end of the season, finishing 17th in MLB with a 4.24 ERA. Probably half a run separated the Orioles from an actually good rotation. Some of that could have been helped with better defense. Some of it could have been helped by better pitching. As things look right now, the rotation is lined up with Kyle Bradish, Shane Baz, Brandon Young, Cade Povich, and Trey Gibson. That’s what is on FanGraphs projected depth chart and I think it seems like a good enough guess. That’s a bad rotation picture unless Povich or Gibson pulls off a Young-like turnaround into 2027, and it’s not even really guaranteed that Young stays turned around. The needs are pretty much the same as they were going into last offseason. They need to reinforce the front end and they need to reinforce the back end too. Last year, the front end reinforcement was trading for Baz; with a 4.11 ERA, he was no help at the front end. The back end reinforcements were Chris Bassitt and Zach Eflin. The Orioles lost Eflin for the season in the middle of his first start, which isn’t Mike Elias’s fault but that bad luck still hurt the team. Bassitt’s 4.59 ERA didn’t help the back end too much in the aggregate, though he was better after returning from back surgery. They’re going to have to do better about it this year. Does Elias have it in him? If he has it in him, will he be able to show it before the lockout hits in December? These are the questions that will be lingering all month until they are either addressed in some affirmative way or the lockout hits and shows the answer is no. Given his track record, I don’t blame anybody for feeling anxious about it. top.title: Cowboys news: The lack of snaps for George Pickens explained
top.description: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images If the Cowboys are going to find themselves in any kind of position to win a bad NFC East division, their defense has got to improve. Multiple players have spoken about the state of the unit, and the solutions don’t seem to be that difficult, but they have to put it all together on the field. One of the big topics around Dallas lately has been wide receiver George Pickens and his playing time, or lack thereof. There’s been speculation as to why this is, but it was recently cleared up by head coach Brian Schottenheimer. Brian Schottenheimer Explains George Pickens’ Lack of Snaps, Targets in Recent Cowboys Games – Mike Moraitis, SI.com The reduction of snaps for Pickens has been very noticeable over the last few weeks. Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer breaks down why that’s been the case. “Brian Schottenheimer told me that George Pickens snaps have been limited by his injuries,” Clarence Hill of DLLS Cowboys said. “He has been taken off the field because blocking in the run game.” Schottenheimer added that it “would be poor coaching by me” to keep Pickens off the field for any reason. That checks out because Pickens was added to the injury report in Week 7 due to a shoulder issue and he remained on it through last week. Cowboys defense searching for answers after meltdown loss: ‘Execute on Sunday’ – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram The Cowboys defense has had trouble with consistency in 2026. According to defensive tackle Quinnen Williams, the solution is quite simple. top.title: Eisenkot tipped to seek Israel government as religious party drops Netanyahu
top.description: Gadi Eisenkot emerged on Thursday as the favourite to be tasked with trying to form an Israeli government as a religious party long aligned with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declined to recommend him. President Isaac Herzog was holding a second day of consultations with political parties after the October 27 election, in which neither Netanyahu — a polarising right-winger who has led Israel through three years of war — nor Eisenkot — a former military chief promising to restore national unity — secured enough votes for a majority. Herzog will choose by himself whom to ask to form a new government but traditionally the mandate is given to the person recommended by more parties, which would be Eisenkot. The opposition leader also received a recommendation from a key lawmaker from the Israeli-Arab minority, whose seats in parliament soared due to outrage over Netanyahu’s policies, even as Eisenkot has remained unclear on whether he would accept Arab support to form a government. United Torah Judaism, which backed Netanyahu after the previous five elections, in its meeting with Herzog declined to recommend Netanyahu again as prime minister, although it also did not side with Eisenkot. The party informed Herzog “that it has decided not to recommend any member of Knesset to form a government,” the president’s office said in a statement, referring to the 120-member parliament in which United Torah Judaism has won seven seats. The party — which represents ultra-Orthodox Jews of Ashkenazi origin, who mostly hail from or have roots in Europe — as well as Shas — which represents the same community but of Sephardic, or mostly Middle Eastern and North African descent — have both been backed by Netanyahu as they push to maintain the exemption from military service for religious students. nigeria.title: Leave EFCC out of politics, Kogi group warns Obi-Kwankwaso Movement
nigeria.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — The Kogi Central Progressive Elites have warned the Obi-Kwankwaso Movement against dragging the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) into partisan politics following its call for an investigation into Senator Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan’s recent cash empowerment programme. The group described the call as a politically motivated attempt to undermine the lawmaker ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a statement issued in Abuja on Thursday, its President, Abdullahi Omeiza, said the group was concerned about what it described as the growing tendency among political actors to deploy anti-corruption institutions and rhetoric for partisan purposes. He said: “We are concerned about the growing tendency among some political actors to deploy anti-corruption institutions and rhetoric as instruments of partisan warfare. “Accountability is important, but it must be pursued through facts, evidence and established legal procedures, not through sensational political narratives designed to damage the reputation of an elected public official.” The group argued that constituency empowerment programmes should not automatically be classified as vote-buying simply because they involve direct financial assistance to beneficiaries. It said such initiatives could be subjected to legitimate scrutiny, but insisted that any investigation must be guided by evidence and the law. “The mere distribution of financial assistance to constituents does not, in itself, establish an offence of vote-buying,” the statement added. On the demand for an EFCC investigation and prosecution, the group acknowledged that no one was above the law but cautioned against turning anti-corruption agencies into instruments of political intimidation. Omeiza said: “Accountability is indispensable to democratic governance, but it must never become a convenient weapon for settling political scores. “Allegations are not convictions, petitions are not proof of wrongdoing, and public accusations cannot substitute for due process. “The EFCC must be allowed to discharge its statutory responsibilities independently, without being subjected to political pressure or media-driven prejudgement.” The group challenged the Obi-Kwankwaso Movement to submit any credible evidence to the appropriate authorities rather than rely on public declarations and what it described as inflammatory narratives. It also maintained that the people of Kogi Central had the right to assess Akpoti-Uduaghan’s performance and determine whether she deserved another term. “The people of Kogi Central are politically conscious, discerning and capable of evaluating their representative. One of the victims, identified as Dapo, is a recently discharged corps member who completed his national service in Edo State last week. She said her brother had been updating the family about his journey until he sent a video showing the traffic situation on the road, which turned out to be their last communication with him. nigeria.title: UK to hold talks on harms of slave trade
nigeria.description: Commonwealth leaders have welcomed Britain’s agreement to engage in “time-bound inclusive and good-faith dialogue” over the “historical harms” of the transatlantic slave trade. In a final communique issued late on Wednesday, the group of nations said the time had come for “meaningful, truthful and respectful conversation towards forging a common future based on equity”. But it did not set out a timetable for the talks. It comes after British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he was open to saying sorry but ruled out paying financial reparations demanded by some Caribbean countries. Burnham used his appearance at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda to hold discussions about issuing a formal apology for Britain’s role in slavery, which saw about 10-15 million slaves brought from Africa to the Americas over four centuries. In a speech to opening the biannual Commonwealth leaders meeting on Tuesday, King Charles III, who is politically neutral, called the slave trade “a monstrous injustice” that filled him with “profound personal sorrow”, stopping short of a formal apology. Britain’s pivotal part in slavery has long strained relations between the UK and its former colonies, including an awkward previous meeting of Commonwealth leaders in 2024. “We welcome the agreement of the government of the United Kingdom to engage in a structured, time-bound, inclusive and good-faith dialogue with affected parties addressing the transatlantic trafficking of enslaved Africans and its historical harms,” the final communique said. The Commonwealth is a 56-nation group of mostly former British colonies. Of those Charles remains head of state in 14. Britain’s Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has said it is “not feasible” for the country to pay reparations for slavery, but that “there are things we can work on co-operatively”. Miliband also hinted that Britain could issue a formal apology next year when it hosts a G20 leaders’ summit, in comments to the BBC aired on Wednesday as the meeting wrapped up. nigeria.title: Kane becomes highest-paid footballer in Europe after new deal
nigeria.description: England captain Harry Kane has signed a record-breaking contract extension with Bayern Munich that will keep him at the German club until June 2029, in a deal reportedly making him the highest-paid player in Europe by basic salary. According to David Ornstein of The Athletic , the three-year extension is the most lucrative contract in Bayern Munich’s history, although some European players could still earn more than the striker when performance-related bonuses are included. The 33-year-old’s previous contract was due to expire next summer, but both Kane and the Bundesliga champions were keen to continue their partnership. Bayern reportedly do not consider the new agreement his final contract, with the club keen to retain the England international for the foreseeable future. Speaking after signing the extension, Kane expressed his satisfaction with life in Munich, describing his relationship with the club, supporters and city as a special one. “I feel right at home at FC Bayern. I love the club, the fans and the city of Munich,” he said. “We have a fantastic team and, in Vincent Kompany, a fantastic manager. It makes me very proud to be part of this club. My whole family is very happy here. I was keen to stay. “I’m now looking forward to the future and I want to win many more titles with this great club.” The contract extension comes after a remarkable period for the striker, who won the Ballon d’Or in late October, becoming the first English player to receive the prestigious award since 2001. He is also expected to become England’s most-capped player during the November international break. Since joining Bayern from Tottenham Hotspur three years ago, Kane has scored 156 goals in 161 appearances, establishing himself as one of the club’s most influential players. During his time in Germany, he has won two Bundesliga titles, the DFB-Pokal and two Supercups. However, winning the UEFA Champions League remains a major ambition for the England captain as he looks to add Europe’s biggest club competition to his collection of honours. His decision to extend his stay in Germany also appears to have dealt a significant blow to hopes of him returning to the Premier League to challenge Alan Shearer’s all-time scoring record. With his Bayern future secured until 2029, Kane looks increasingly likely to prioritise further success in Germany over a return to English football. nigeria.title: Wike distances self from court ruling favouring Okorocha over Uzodimma
nigeria.description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has dismissed claims that he influenced the court judgment which recognised former Imo State Governor Rochas Okorocha as the All Progressives Congress candidate for Imo West Senatorial District in the 2027 elections. Wike spoke during a live media chat on Thursday in Port Harcourt, where he described the allegations as mischievous, stressing that he neither filed the suit nor had any involvement in the legal proceedings. “First of all, anybody calling my name is being mischievous. I didn’t go to court. I’m not in APC. I don’t know what the issue is,” he said. Wike also reacted to reports that Governor Hope Uzodimma had warned, a day before the judgment, that he would seize the vehicles of anyone promoting the proposed Rainbow Coalition in Imo State. Describing the reported warning as uncivilised, the minister said: “They were saying that because a day before that judgment was given, he had openly warned people that, ‘No Rainbow Coalition here. If I see… I’ll collect the vehicle for you.’ Very, very uncivilised.” He also clarified a video circulating online showing him dancing with Okorocha, saying it was recorded when he hosted the former governor while he was still in office. “Now they showed the video where Rochas and I danced when I hosted him when he was governor. So that was that dance,” Wike said. The controversy followed a Federal High Court judgment in Abuja directing the Independent National Electoral Commission to recognise Okorocha as the APC candidate for Imo West Senatorial District in the 2027 general election. Justice Obiora Egwuatu ruled that Okorocha emerged winner of the party’s senatorial primary held on May 18, 2026, rather than Uzodimma, and ordered INEC to substitute the governor’s name with that of the former governor. The case was instituted by Okorocha, who challenged INEC’s recognition of Uzodimma as the winner of the primary. The court held that the evidence presented showed that Okorocha secured the majority of valid votes cast. The ruling has been contested by the Imo State chapter of the APC, while Uzodimma has indicated plans to appeal. nigeria.title: Cristiano Ronaldo retires from international football
nigeria.description: Portuguese football legend Cristiano Ronaldo announced on Thursday that he was retiring from international football at the age of 41. Ronaldo played 234 times for Portugal and scored 146 goals — a world record. But the forward’s powers have been waning in recent years and he fell out with national coach Jorge Jesus last month after he refused to play him in a Nations League match. Ronaldo immediately left the team camp and was handed a 30-day suspension. Although it was rumoured that he intended to return to the international fold, on Thursday the five-time winner of the Ballon d’Or released a video on his Instagram account in which he said he was ending his international career. “To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt of our national team,” Ronaldo said, as images of his career were played. “I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world,” he continued. “Today the time has come to pass it on to the future. It was not an easy decision, because some decisions are not made with the mind alone — they are also made with the heart. “A journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end,” he added. In the highlight of his international career, Ronaldo won the European Championship with Portugal in 2016 in France, although he had to leave the field during the final with an injury. At this year’s World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico, he scored three goals but Portugal were knocked out in the Round of 16 by eventual winners Spain. nigeria.title: Zelensky says hopes US election means more support for Ukraine
nigeria.description: Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky has said he hoped the Democrat triumph in the US midterm elections would boost support for Kyiv and help end the war with Russia. Ukraine and its European allies had been worried about the United States getting closer to Russia since President Donald Trump returned to the White House last year. Ties between Trump and Zelensky have been turbulent, with tensions rising in recent weeks as the US leader criticised Kyiv and made a deal with President Vladimir Putin to ease sanctions in return for the release of Russian diesel. “There is hope now that there is this balance of power, and that we will be supported more,” Zelensky told German broadcaster ZDF in an interview broadcast late Wednesday. Zelensky said that if the US Congress “starts talking about strong financial support or military support” it would “influence Putin.” “And Putin will be thinking about whether it makes sense to keep fighting if the support will only grow. Logically, this will (lead) us to possible negotiations and a possible peace,” he said. US-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks are to be held next week in Abu Dhabi. The talks had been frozen since the Middle East war erupted in February. Trump’s special envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner have been leading the negotiations amid criticism over their attitude to Russia. nigeria.title: Court sacks Mark-led ADC exco, voids Atiku’s candidacy
nigeria.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Abuja The Federal High Court in Abuja has sacked the Senator David Mark-led executives of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and invalidated all actions they took on behalf of the party. The actions included the nomination of a former vice president, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, as the party’s presidential candidate for the 2027 general elections. Atiku, whose name was earlier published by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) as a candidate for the presidential poll, has since chosen a former governor of Rivers State, Rotimi Amaechi, as his running mate. However, in a judgment delivered on Thursday by Justice Peter Lifu, the court declared illegal the Senator Mark-led Caretaker Committee of the ADC, which organised the primary election that produced Atiku as the party’s presidential flag bearer. The court found merit in a suit brought before it by the aggrieved former National Deputy Chairman (North-East) of the party, Nafiu Bala Gombe. Gombe had approached the court to query the process through which the Senator Mark-led Committee took over the reins of leadership of the party. He maintained that, with the resignation of the former National Chairman, Chief Ralph Nwosu, he (Gombe) was qualified to assume the party’s leadership. Consequently, he, among other things, prayed the court to nullify all actions taken on behalf of the party by the Senator Mark-led leadership. Listed as defendants in the suit, marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1819/2025, were the ADC, INEC, Senator Mark, Ogbeni Rauf Aregbesola and Chief Ralph Nwosu. The plaintiff further urged the court to restrain Senator Mark and Aregbesola from parading themselves as National Chairman and Secretary, respectively, of the ADC, insisting that their emergence violated the party’s constitution and the provisions of the Electoral Act. The court upheld the plaintiff’s claim and granted his reliefs, a verdict that could spark a chain of reactions in the polity, with the presidential election scheduled for January 16, 2027. Already, the ADC has vowed to appeal the judgment. Reacting to the outcome of the case, the National Welfare Secretary of the ADC, Mr. Nkemakolam Ukandu, who was later joined as an interested party in the matter, said the verdict would be challenged at the appellate court. The development comes barely 24 hours after the party’s candidate, Atiku, held a massive rally in Sokoto State as part of his campaign for the 2027 presidential election. nigeria.title: Netanyahu loses religious party’s support as rival tipped to form government
nigeria.description: An ultra-Orthodox Jewish party long aligned with Benjamin Netanyahu declined on Thursday to recommend him to stay as Israel’s prime minister, as signs grew that rival Gadi Eisenkot will have the first chance to form a government. President Isaac Herzog was holding a second day of consultations with political parties after the October 27 election, in which neither Netanyahu — a polarising right-winger who has led Israel through three years of war — nor Eisenkot secured enough votes for a majority. United Torah Judaism, which backed Netanyahu after the previous five elections, in its meeting with Herzog declined to recommend Netanyahu again as prime minister, although it also did not side with Eisenkot. The party informed Herzog “that it has decided not to recommend any member of Knesset to form a government,” the president’s office said in a statement, referring to the 120-member parliament in which United Torah Judaism has won seven seats. The party, which represents ultra-Orthodox Jews of Ashkenazi origin, who mostly hail from or have roots in Europe, as well as Shas, which represents the same community but of Sephardic, or mostly Middle Eastern and North African descent, have both been backed by Netanyahu as they push to maintain the exemption from military service for religious students. Netanyahu has preserved the exemption but stopped short of enshrining it in law, in the face of major resentment from many other Israelis as reservists serve multiple tours due to the wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. “In whatever government is next formed, our immediate item is sorting out the status of Torah students,” United Torah Judaism lawmaker Isaac Pindrus said. Eisenkot, a former military chief seeking to unite the centre and centre-right, has been adamant about closing exemptions to military service, with some of his opposition allies harshly criticising the ultra-Orthodox as self-serving. Observers say United Torah Judaism’s approach may be aimed more at punishing Netanyahu and showing that their votes cannot be taken for granted, while they could still serve in a government if he were to form one. Herzog will meet representatives of the major parties later on Thursday before tasking one lawmaker with forming a government. He generally bases his decision on which person receives the most party recommendations, making it likely he will ask Eisenkot. Once Herzog gives the mandate, that lawmaker will have 28 days to form a government, with a potential 14-day extension. If the lawmaker fails, Herzog will then task someone else. Netanyahu’s bloc — including United Torah Judaism — has 53 seats in the new parliament, as opposed to 48 for Eisenkot’s bloc. Israeli-Arab parties soared in strength on the back of anger over Netanyahu’s hard-right government, winning 19 seats. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Houston Rockets fell to the Minnesota Timberwolves 117-107. (Elizabeth Conley/Houston Chronicle) Down the final stretch of Wednesday night's matchup with the Minnesota Timberwolves, Houston Rockets coach Ime Udoka toggled between a few different lineups. Udoka played his usual starting five - Fred VanVleet, Amen Thompson, Jabari Smith Jr., Kevin Durant and Alperen Şengün - for a little more than two minutes. He went to a small-ball variation with Tari Eason in Şengün's place for about 90 seconds, then put Sengun back in for Smith to close out the final 2:10, according to FadeAway's lineup data. What led to the changes? "Trying to get a stop," Udoka said. ROCKETS MAILBAG: Can Amen Thompson touch the top of the backboard? Houston couldn't get enough stops, giving up 35 points in a fourth quarter it lost by 12 en route to its second defeat of the season, 117-107, at Toyota Center. The Timberwolves, playing without star Anthony Edwards, got a strong late-game showing from point guard LaMelo Ball. Udoka said the Rockets did a good job guarding Ball for about three and a half quarters, and he was right. Ball scored 12 of his 20 points and had two of his six assists in the final seven minutes. "I just think we were too loose on them the whole game and they got going," said Durant, who led Houston with 21 points but was one of three Rockets - along with Şengün and VanVleet - with four turnovers. Giveaways were a major problem Wednesday, with 22 Houston miscues leading to 33 Minnesota points. Udoka said the Rockets had poor awareness when kicking the ball out after touching the paint against a Timberwolves defense that routinely sent help. sports.title: Three of the biggest threats to a Notre Dame victory over Miami
sports.description: SOUTH BEND, INDIANA - OCTOBER 10: CJ Carr #13 of the Notre Dame Fighting Irish runs the ball against the Stanford Cardinal at Notre Dame Stadium on October 10, 2026 in South Bend, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images Saturday is rapidly approaching and we are all eager to see how Notre Dame responds to the recent challenge laid before them by the college football playoff committee — beat Miami or plan on watching the playoffs from home. But what obstacles lay in Notre Dame’s way? What are some of the biggest threats to that victory? MISCOMMUNICATION Despite the loss of wide receiver Malachi Toney, Miami still has a potent offense, and the Irish need to play much better on defense than they did against BYU. One of the big issues in that loss was the lack of communication or just plain miscommunication on defense. Assignments were blown, and the Irish looked lost at times. We saw similar things in losses to Miami and Texas A&M last year. If Notre Dame can’t play with more discipline and poise, they could suffer the same fate. THE SLOW START In most pf the games Notre Dame has lost during the Marcus Freeman era, we see that the team tends to come out flat — and more than that even. They’re flat, timid, confused, and even overzealous. They work themselves into a hole, and then spend two or more quarters trying to overcome its beginning nonsense. If the Irish can come out swinging and kind of “catch that groove” early, things should work in their favor, but if not… it will be a much MUCH heavier load (especially with the weight of the stakes of this game). COWARDLY PLAY Don’t do it. Do NOT get regrettably conservative. CJ Carr has that issue during most games, and it’s like he’s too afraid to make a mistake — so he overthrows a guy here and then under throws a guy there. He doesn’t turn the ball over , and that’s definitely important, but in a game like this — he needs to unleash himself. That can be accomplished by Freeman having a conversation with him and Mike Denbrock. In that same conversation, Freeman can remind both that Carr has legs, and despite not using them much this season — maybe Saturday would be a good time to use them a bit more. Don’t be cowards — do something different.

Originally signing with Oklahoma, he started five games for the Sooners at left guard before transferring back to his home state. Everyone has their own different level of pessimism for how likely it is that MLB’s owner-imposed lockout of the players will end by then in order to allow the season to begin. How you feel about the Orioles rotation minus Trevor Rogers probably has a lot to do with how much urgency you think the team should have this offseason. The team had a “could have been worse” rotation in 2026 even with Rogers being as good as he was from about June on to the end of the season, finishing 17th in MLB with a 4.24 ERA. Probably half a run separated the Orioles from an actually good rotation. Some of that could have been helped with better defense. Some of it could have been helped by better pitching. As things look right now, the rotation is lined up with Kyle Bradish, Shane Baz, Brandon Young, Cade Povich, and Trey Gibson. That’s a bad rotation picture unless Povich or Gibson pulls off a Young-like turnaround into 2027, and it’s not even really guaranteed that Young stays turned around. The needs are pretty much the same as they were going into last offseason. They need to reinforce the front end and they need to reinforce the back end too. Does Elias have it in him? If he has it in him, will he be able to show it before the lockout hits in December? These are the questions that will be lingering all month until they are either addressed in some affirmative way or the lockout hits and shows the answer is no. sports.title: NY Giants cornerback Greg Newsome: Defense is ‘perfect scheme for me’
sports.description: New York Giants cornerback Greg Newsome II intercepts a pass against the Arizona Cardinals. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New York Giants secondary was widely looked at as one of team’s weaknesses coming into the 2026 season. The Giants were widely expected to make a splash to rebuild a unit that disappointed in 2025, but instead they merely brought in cornerback Greg Newsome II. Newsome II was a former first round pick by the Browns, but his career stalled in Cleveland and he was traded by the Browns to the Jacksonville Jaguars in 2025. So he was looked at as a flier at best when he signed a one-year deal with the Giants in the spring of 2026. At least that’s how the media at large viewed him. Newsome still saw himself as a first round corner and was willing to bet on himself if he could land in the right situation. Six games later, Newsome has signed a three-year, $46 million extension to make New York his home through the 2029 season. “I believed wholeheartedly after I signed a one-year,” he said on Wednesday. “I knew the type of person I was, first and foremost. And I knew what type of player I was and I knew that if I just get to the right place, that the money will take care of itself. I feel like when you’re somewhere that you’re wanted, you’re somewhere that you’re loved, everything else takes care of itself. So, I knew this would be the place.” He added that he was very intentional in wanting to come play for John Harbaugh and the New York Giants. “My first thing was fit,” Newsome said. “What coaches know me, and that was the biggest thing. I obviously played against Harbs a lot, so he knew what type of player I was, and I knew what type of coach he was. So, that was kind of my first thing, alright, fit. How did his defenses play in the past? Because that’s going to be kind of how the defense will be playing in New York.” From there, Newsome decided to bet on himself in big market. He knew a “Ravens” style defense would fit his skill set, and that the city would be a fit as well as the coach and system. “So, I figured, how about I sign in one year?” he added. “How about I come to New York and just play in front of a big media outlet? I feel like my personality will be able to show more in this city. So, that was kind of my thought process. “I think it starts from the top down,” he said when asked what makes the Giants such a great fit. “Starting obviously with ownership, just how they carry themselves. sports.description: Cristiano Ronaldo became the first player to win five Champions League trophies and remains the top scorer in the tournament's history [Getty Images] Cristiano Ronaldo says his international career with Portugal is over, meaning the 41-year-old will just play on with Al-Nassr. The main thing driving him on now is hoping to reach an unprecedented 1,000 career goals - he is currently on 985. BBC Sport looks at some of the most iconic moments of a career that has also taken in spells at Sporting, Manchester United, Real Madrid and Juventus. Ronaldo retires from Portugal duty Ronaldo spurred on by 1,000 goals and Portugal glory Ronaldo will not retire until he scores 1,000 goals Untouchable or a support act? Ronaldo's 1,000-goal quest continues The friendly that changed everything After 31 first-team games and five goals for Sporting, Ronaldo caught the eye of Manchester United in a pre-season friendly in 2003, setting up two goals in a 3-1 win in Lisbon. Ronaldo revealed that United boss Alex Ferguson took him into the dressing room afterwards to meet the players. Five days later he joined the Red Devils for £12m. "After we played Sporting the lads in the dressing room talked about him constantly, and on the plane back from the game they urged me to sign him - that's how highly they rated him," said Ferguson. "He is one of the most exciting young players I've ever seen." Ronaldo wins first Premier League title (2007) Cristiano Ronaldo has won league titles in England, Spain, Italy and Saudi Arabia [Getty Images] Ronaldo won the FA Cup in his first season at United, scoring in the final against Millwall. But it was in 2006-07 that his career really exploded. Also important was the bridge between modern analytics in the cloud and on-prem or hosted legacy systems such as ECC, the ERP system broadly adopted by global companies. technology.title: When datacenters lose power, generators should kick in. That didn’t happen for Google in London
technology.description: Google Cloud has revealed that the cause of the October 20 outage in its europe-west-2-b availability zone was a ‘misconfiguration’ of its systems that meant its emergency generators didn’t start. The outage at the London facility caused service interruptions at outfits including Lloyds, HSBC, Royal Mail, and Revolut. In a November 4 update to its service status page, Google explained what went wrong. “The site relies on a 2N utility power architecture — where the facility has complete duplicate power paths for every critical load — backed by a central high-voltage generator bank managed by a dual-redundant Programmable Logic Controller (PLC),” Google revealed. The facility gets its juice from two independent utility feeders, which Google calls “A” and “B”. There’s also a “standby utility connection configured for manual campus-wide transfer during maintenance operations or emergency events.” Google says the root cause of the incident was failure in an external underground cable through which its power supplier brings ‘leccy to its bit barns. That cable connects to primary feeder A and it broke at a time when feeder B wasn’t working. “Circuit breaker feeder B was physically opened to allow for corrective repairs following issues identified during a quarterly generator load test on 14 Oct 2026,” Google admitted. “Consequently, primary utility feed A was supporting the total critical load while the feed B breaker remained in an open position to allow repairs to be conducted on the B feeder pathway.” That shouldn’t be a problem for a top-tier operator like Google, which knows it needs to install backup sources of electricity like uninterruptible power supplies (UPS) and on-site generators. Indeed, europe-west-2-b employs UPSes that Google says can keep things up and running for five minutes if the availability zone loses its connection to the grid. The UPSes worked, but a “voltage-sensing design flaw and PLC misconfiguration prevented the facility’s generator plant from receiving an automatic start signal to assume the critical load.” Google’s UPSes therefore ran out of juice, but its generators didn’t start. The rest is history. The search giant has figured out that its PLCs weren’t set up to handle the conditions it faced on this fateful day. “PLC logic indicated that a healthy utility source was available, even though the primary and secondary distribution feeds were de-energized, and did not issue a start command to the generator plant,” the status update reveals. Once Google was able to reconnect to its power utility, it reprogrammed the PLC so it wouldn’t make the same mistake again. The Big G has since made many changes to the electrical setup at europe-west-2-b and says it’s tested them and that they all work. technology.title: Microsoft admits certifications can be a drag, launches creds that recognize skills
technology.description: When The Register writes about professional certifications offered by vendors, we often receive comments arguing that such credentials are nowhere near as valuable as real-world experience. Now, Microsoft has acknowledged there’s some merit in that argument. Redmond revealed its stance last week in a post from general manager for content and insights Cameron Percy, who observed: “For years, people have asked for a simpler way to prove the skills they use in the flow of work, without stepping away to prepare for another test.” Microsoft’s response is the “Pro Badge,” a new form of credential that Percy wrote “works alongside Microsoft Certifications.” “Certifications show that you can solve problems in a role or field. Pro Badge shows how you use a specific product in your everyday work. Together, they give a more complete picture of what you can do.” “Instead of capturing skills on a single test day, this approach keeps pace with your work and the products you use,” Percy added. “It gives you a current, verified signal of what you can do, at no cost and without a separate exam or study guide.” The first Pro Badge is for GitHub Copilot. To earn it, users need only visit learn.github.com and sign in with their GitHub account. Going through those steps fires up a “proficiency engine” that Microsoft says “gets to work analyzing relevant product usage signals and evaluating them against a defined proficiency framework.” Percy’s post says it “systematically uses evidence from everyday product use to calculate and automatically update your proficiency level.” Microsoft offers five levels of proficiency: beginner, intermediate, proficient, advanced, and expert. To earn a Pro Badge, users must reach the proficient level. A beginner has had “first contact” with GitHub and “understands what Copilot is, where it can be used, and how it might fit into everyday development workflows.” An intermediate user is “familiar with web-based collaboration features, core IDE features, model management, agent configuration, customization options, and techniques for managing context.” To score the Pro Badge, users will need to demonstrate “practical ability to work on projects” and use GitHub “across typical scenarios, demonstrated through consistent hands-on usage across multiple repositories and extended periods.” “A Proficient user can use many web and IDE features, select appropriate models, and apply customizations to tailor Copilot for specific project needs. technology.title: Building AI factories at enterprise scale
technology.description: AI has become a juggernaut, driving technical strategy in the tech sector and outside of it. With the worldwide server market growing 30 percent in a single year to hit $122.6bn in the first quarter of 2025, IDC now feels safe recategorizing AI-driven investment "from cyclical to durable". The analyst company expects inference to account for over 70 percent of computing demand by next year, adding that it's growing fastest at the edge. Why enterprises are building their own All this investment in AI infrastructure might once have come mainly for hyperscalers, but that's changing quickly. Adoption is spreading quickly beyond public cloud service providers into enterprise environments, IDC adds. They're eager to run agentic AI in-house. There are plenty of reasons for companies to own their own AI infrastructure rather than offloading it to the cloud. One of these is data control, especially in regulated sectors such as finance, healthcare, manufacturing, and the public sector that have sovereign data requirements. Another revolves around the need for predictable costing from tokens delivered on tunable in-house systems. So what should companies look for in a supplier? Delivery speed will be a powerful driver for many who are under the gun to deliver AI initiatives for the business, especially during periods of constrained memory and CPU supply. Life cycle services will also come near the top of the list, for companies that need help managing everything from the power through to the reasoning LLM models and the workloads that use them. That need for expertise is unlikely to stop; companies will undergo changes in AI strategy as they get to grips with a still-evolving technology. From the desk to the datacenter ASUS expects this AI surge to continue in the datacenter, but elsewhere too, specifically in edge locations (especially industrial use cases) and at developers' desks, as the applications that will power the enterprise get made. It wants to be top of peoples' list for hardware and services at all these places along the AI continuum. At NVIDIA's GTC show in Berlin on Oct 21-22, it announced a full-stack AI offering that it's calling its Enterprise Agentic AI Solution . It's three-layer affair, featuring: ASUS AI Server and Infrastructure: Its selection of AI servers, including several new units. ASUS AI Software Stack: Its software for integrating and controlling AI workflows. ASUS AI HUB: A services operation that ties it all together. These bring together some existing assets that ASUS had for enterprise AI users, along with some new ones. The time is right for an end-to-end offering with new hardware because of the way the market is shifting, say ASUS execs. science.title: 2 astronauts will finish upgrading ISS solar arrays during spacewalk today: Watch it live
science.description: null Two spacewalking astronauts will finish upgrading the International Space Station's power system today (Nov. 5), and you can watch the action live. NASA astronaut Anil Menon and the Canadian Space Agency 's Joshua Kutryk will install the eighth and final International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) today, during a roughly seven-hour spacewalk that's scheduled to begin at 8:30 a.m. EST (1330 GMT). You can watch it live here at Space.com , courtesy of NASA, beginning at 7 a.m. EDT (1200 GMT). NASA astronaut Anil Menon points his camera toward his spacesuit’s helmet visor and takes a selfie during a spacewalk on Oct. 29, 2026. (Image credit: NASA) Today's extravehicular activity (EVA) will be the second in a week for Menon and Kutryk, who installed the station's seventh iROSA during an Oct. 29 spacewalk . That excursion was the 100th U.S. spacewalk from the ISS to date, and the first EVA for a Canadian astronaut since 2019. Today's spacewalk will wrap up an ambitious ISS power upgrade that has taken more than five years to pull off. "The installation job will complete the years-long process that began in June 2021 to augment the space station’s power generating capacity from 160 kilowatts to about 215 kilowatts," NASA officials wrote about the EVA in a blog post on Tuesday (Nov. 3) . That's a boost of about 30%. Menon and Kutryk are currently sharing the ISS with five other astronauts — NASA's Luke Delaney and Jessica Watkins and cosmonauts Pyotr Dubrov, Anna Kikina and Sergey Teteryatnikov. Delaney, Kutryk, Teteryatnikov and Watkins arrived at the ISS on Oct. 1, on SpaceX's Crew-13 mission . Dubrov, Kikina and Menon got there in mid-July, aboard a Russian Soyuz spacecraft.

science.title: Cyprus: Island of Snakes, Cats, and Ophiolites
science.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Cyprus: Island of Snakes,… Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search Seasonal rains had started to fill Akrotiri Salt Lake when the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 8 captured this image of Cyprus’s Akrotiri Peninsula on October 10, 2026. NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison The island of Cyprus began to form some 90 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous , with molten rock pouring from the seafloor, solidifying, and building new oceanic crust . Over time, portions of this oceanic rock were wrenched upward by tectonic forces , eventually emerging as a rugged island made of ophiolite , a type of rock with a mottled green appearance said to look like the skin of a snake. Remnants of that ancient island are still visible in the dark rocks of the Troodos Mountains . During the Miocene , considerably younger layers of chalk, limestone, marl, and other marine sedimentary rocks accumulated around the island, providing material that developed into a second, smaller island to the south during a later period of geologic uplift . Over time, sediment poured from rivers into the channel separating the two islands and combined with marine sediments to create deltas and eventually two land bridges, or tombolos . The joined landmass comprises the Akrotiri Peninsula , now the southernmost tip of Cyprus. The sandy edges of the peninsula were visible when Landsat 8 captured these images on October 10, 2026. Akrotiri Salt Lake , a coastal lagoon that was once an arm of the Mediterranean Sea, lies between the two tombolos. The more westerly feature, the Kouris River tombolo, formed first, developing about 50,000 years ago from river-deposited gravels and sands. The eastern tombolo extended southward from Cyprus, cutting off the Mediterranean Sea only within the past 2,000 years, according to geologists . The lake’s water levels now vary markedly with the seasons, typically filling in the late autumn and winter and drying out in the summer. The influx of winter water has historically attracted sizable overwintering flamingo populations, averaging about 4,000 birds. However, the wintering flamingo population has declined in recent years, plummeting to 30 birds in 2025, according to news reports . Flamingos have long flocked to the lake to feed on fairy shrimp , which are rich in colorful substances called carotenoids that give the birds their famously pink hue . Snakes are another of the island’s more notorious animal inhabitants. In antiquity, Cyprus was known as Ophiousa , or “ land of snakes ,” likely due to its robust population of blunt-nosed vipers . science.title: NASA Announces X-70 Experimental Aircraft to Advance Flight Research
science.description: Generated image of NASA’s new X-70 Fractal experimental aircraft, a crewed, rapidly reconfigurable research platform for advanced aviation technologies. On Wednesday, NASA unveiled its newest experimental aircraft, the X-70 Fractal, during the UP.Summit at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. This high-performance, highly adaptable research platform is designed to accelerate the development and testing of advanced aviation technologies. The crewed X-70 features advanced, rapidly reconfigurable flight-control technology that will allow NASA to explore aircraft maneuverability in ways never before demonstrated in crewed flight. The aircraft can also accommodate up to 2,000 pounds of experimental payloads in internal and external locations, enabling a wide range of research and flight-testing opportunities. “The X-70 Fractal gives NASA a crewed, high-performance platform to test advanced flight-control, maneuverability, and other cutting-edge technologies in real flight,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “Its modular design and ability to rapidly swap internal and external payloads will keep our teams flying, learning, and moving quickly from one experiment to the next. We expect her first flight under the NASA banner within the next two years, and X-70 is just one part of this new beginning for aeronautics. This is why people come to NASA: to build, to learn, and most importantly, to fly.” The X-70 Fractal has a takeoff weight of 10,000 pounds and is designed to cruise at Mach .75, reach altitudes of up to 45,000 feet, and provide an operational range exceeding about 1,726 miles (1,500 nautical miles). These capabilities will enable NASA to conduct demanding flight research across a broad range of operating conditions. “For decades, NASA Aeronautics has used X-planes to develop technologies that advance aviation,” said Laurie Grindle, director of the Aeronautics Division within NASA’s Research and Technology Mission Directorate. “It’s exciting to bring on another X-plane to accelerate and drive aeronautics research.” The X-70 joins a storied legacy of experimental aircraft that have helped establish America’s leadership in aviation. From the Bell X-1, which first broke the sound barrier in 1947, to the X-15 hypersonic research aircraft and today’s X-59 quiet supersonic demonstrator, NASA has spent decades pushing the boundaries of flight. With the X-70, NASA will expand its capacity to conduct experimental flight research, accelerate the testing of emerging technologies, and advance the next generation of American aviation. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 4, 2015: A rail-launched Super Strypi rocket carrying 13 baby satellites failed during its debut launch for the US Air Force
science.description: null On Nov. 4, 2015, the United States Air Force planned to launch an experimental rocket for small satellites from the Pacific Missile Range Facility off Barking Sands, Kauai, Hawaii. The launch didn't according to plan . For this mission, the Air Force was testing out the Super Strypi rocket . The rocket used a rail to help with the liftoff. Super Strypi left the ground, but the rocket quickly spun out of control. When it crashed, it destroyed all of the tiny satellites riding aboard the rocket. The cause? Likely a problem with the first stage motor. The mission lost 13 tiny satellites known as cubesats. Cubesats are a popular option for space missions, because they are small and cheap, and they often operate in swarms. After failing to launch this batch of cubesats, the Super Strypi program never recovered from its failure, and the Air Force never tried launching another one. The U.S. Air Force’s rail-launched Super Strypi rocket lifted off from Hawaii about 9:45 p.m. local time on Nov. 3, 2015,, roared toward the sky and failed less than a minute into the long-awaited flight. (Image credit: U.S. Air Force) Why it mattered The Super Strypi rocket was a 21st century take on a 1960s rocket. It was designed to be a modern version of the three-stage Strypi sounding rocket used for for reentry vehicle and anti-missile target tests. Its three stages, powered by Aerojet Rocketdyne solid rocket motors, was designed to reach orbit, rather than suborbital trajectories common to most sounding rockets. The U.S. Air Force hoped Super Strypi would be a new tool for quick-response launches based on national security needs. Altogether, it was designed to launch small payloads of up to 300 kilograms into space for a mere $15 million per mission . The rocket's primary payload was the ORS-4 satellite, short for Operationally Responsive Space 4, which was built for the Air Force by engineers at the University of Hawaii (who nicknamed it HiakaSat). It was designed to capture Earth imagery and monitor the environment over the course of a year. The 12 other payloads on Super Strypi included eight cubesats for NASA's Edison Demonstration of Smallsat Networks mission, and as well as four others for universities that had been added as secondary payloads. Since the Super Strypi failure, neither the Air Force or Space Force has opted to use the rocket for a new mission. The Space Force has turned instead to commercial companies for fast-turnaround launch support. In June of this year, the U.S. Space Force teamed up with Rocket Lab to launch the Victus Haze mission with just 17 hours of notice , a new record to demonstrate short-turnaround launch response.

science.title: Trump declares 'American space superiority for all eternity' in election night proclamation
science.description: null President Trump issued a declaration yesterday (Nov. 3), proclaiming space open to all humanity for exploration, and the right of American citizens to develop and settle the solar system according to United States laws. "The American Declaration of Freedom in Space," describes space as the "province of all humans" and asserts that the United States will lead humanity's expansion into the cosmos. The proclamation reiterates the administration's goals with NASA's Artemis program to return American astronauts to the moon by 2028 and eventually sending astronauts to Mars , but introduces no new funding, programs or policy directives. "Our Nation will lead the way in the exploration, development, use, and settlement of these new frontiers — forging an interplanetary civilization founded on the enduring and inalienable rights of freedom and individual liberty," the document says. Trump invoked America's "frontier spirit," highlighting Apollo 11 astronauts as the first people in history to walk on the moon's surface and robotic rovers exploring Mars as examples of U.S. leadership, and emphasized the country's flourishing commercial space sector helping ensure "American space superiority for all eternity." "The nation that leads in space will shape the future of humanity," the declaration says, and pledges that America will carry the values of faith, freedom and individual liberty into an interplanetary civilization. The proclamation also highlights the success of NASA's Artemis II mission in April, which carried four astronauts on a 10-day journey around the moon and set a record for the farthest humans have ever traveled from Earth . The follow-up to that mission, Artemis III, is scheduled to launch next summer (2027), and will test rendezvous and docking operations between NASA's Orion spacecraft and the program's two commercial lunar landers in low Earth orbit . Artemis IV will be the program's first lunar landing mission, and is targeted for 2028. A December 2025 executive order from the President reaffirmed the goal of meeting that timeline, as well as the deployment of the initial elements for a permanent lunar outpost by 2030. Trump's declaration yesterday does not establish new NASA programs, allocate additional funding or issue instructions to federal agencies. Its sweeping language, though, does echo some of the principles in the 1967 Outer Space Treaty , which guarantees freedom of exploration while prohibiting national sovereignty claims on other planets.

Building on the priorities announced at Ignition earlier this year, NASA leadership shared the agency’s significant progress across its missions, working with industry partners to test critical capabilities, reduce risk, and build toward a sustained American presence on the Moon. science.description:
Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

When "Star Trek" celebrated its 60th anniversary in September, it was a strangely muted affair. Sure, there were fan events, screenings, and even an attempt at a world record for the biggest simultaneous Vulcan salute in history , but the lack of a "Doctor Who"-style birthday episode felt like a glaring omission. It was like everyone had shown up for the party, but the organizers had forgotten to book the headline entertainment. Luckily, there were rather more fireworks for the show's 30th birthday, when both "Voyager" and "Deep Space Nine" marked the occasion in style. "Voyager" episode "Flashback" took Tuvok (Tim Russ) back to his days on the USS Excelsior bridge alongside Original Series vets Hikaru Sulu (George Takei) and Janice Rand (Grace Lee Whitney). But it was "DS9"'s "Trials and Tribble-ations" that turned out to be the more memorable voyage to "Trek" past, as Captain Benjamin Sisko (Avery Brooks) — with the help of some then-state-of-the-art digital trickery — came face-to-face with a young Captain James T. Kirk (William Shatner). While "Flashback" aired within days of "Trek"'s September 8 birthday, fans had to wait a little longer for "DS9"'s contribution to the celebrations. Showrunner Ira Steven Behr was keen to avoid disrupting the space station-set drama's story arc for a comedic diversion, meaning that "Trials and Tribble-ations" didn't debut until November 4, 1996. science.title: NASA's Swift space telescope crashes back to Earth after failed rescue attempt
science.description: null NASA's Swift space telescope has reached the end of its long and winding road. Swift fell uncontrolled to Earth today (Nov. 4), 22 years after it launched but just three months after a private spacecraft was supposed to boost it to a higher, life-extending orbit. The 3,200-pound (1,450 kilograms) observatory reentered Earth's atmosphere at 7:39 a.m. EST (1239 GMT) today over northern Sumatra, according to satellite tracker Jonathan McDowell , who cited U.S. Space Force data. The fall likely didn't make much of an impact; NASA officials predicted beforehand that most of the minibus-sized Swift would burn up as it fell, and they put the odds of any of the surviving pieces hurting anyone on Earth at just 1 in 2,100. Several videos circulating on social media appear to show the spacecraft's fiery reentry, though it has yet to be independently verified. Likely reentry of @NASA's #Swift observatory over Sumatra & Malaysia at 12:39 UTC today. November 4, 2026 Likely reentry of @NASA's #Swift observatory over Sumatra & Malaysia at 12:39 UTC today. November 4, 2026 Swift — officially known as the Swift Gamma-Ray Burst Explorer — launched to Earth orbit in November 2004 on a two-year mission to study gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), the most powerful explosions in the universe . "Swift" was not an acronym but rather referred to the spacecraft's observational agility. "Swift needed to detect and locate gamma-ray bursts, communicate their position to other observatories, and then swing its telescopes around to image the burst locations before their afterglows faded out," S. Bradley Cenko, Swift's principal investigator (PI) at NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center in Maryland, said in an Oct. 23 statement . "This typically took Swift about a minute to do." Swift didn't just observe GRBs. It also studied a variety of other cosmic bodies and phenomena, from faraway supernova explosions and feeding black holes to asteroids and comets in our own solar system. And it kept doing this long after its warranty expired — for about 20 years after, in fact. The space telescope didn't conduct its final science observation until this past Oct. 20 . (Swift underwent a name change during this stretch: In 2018, it was rechristened the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory after its first PI, who died the previous year.) "Swift delivered an incredible, lasting return on investment for the nation, designed for a two-year primary mission but productive for more than 10 times as long," Shawn Domagal-Goldman, director of NASA's Astrophysics Division, said in the same Oct. 23 statement. "In that time, Swift played a major role in advancing our understanding of the changing universe and was part of a revolution in astrophysics that showed how critical rapid-response observations are to the entire community," he added. science.title: Toothbrush that emits electricity may more effectively prevent gum disease
science.description: A new and improved toothbrush could help avoid trips to the dentist Westend61/Alamy A toothbrush that generates electricity may more effectively fight harmful bacteria, while removing plaque, than existing products. The toothbrush uses special bristles that produce electricity as they bend, triggering the formation of molecules that damage bacterial membranes. When put to the test, it led to more than twice the reduction of plaque, gum inflammation and bleeding as conventional toothbrushes. “The concept is great,” says Nicholas Jakubovics at Newcastle University, UK, who wasn’t involved in the research. “Basically, the mechanical forces recharge the surface, so it’s really innovative. Anything that even slightly improves the way dental care works could have a benefit, because oral disease is just so widespread.” Read more How regrowing your own teeth could replace dentures and implants Oral diseases, such as tooth decay, affect nearly half the global population . Brushing regularly can help remove plaque, a sticky layer of bacteria that forms on teeth. These bacteria can produce acids that cause cavities and irritate gums, sometimes leading to tooth loss. Advertisement But even thorough brushing can leave behind bacteria deep in plaque or between teeth, allowing colonies to grow back within hours. Researchers have previously developed toothbrushes with antibacterial metal nanoparticles, including silver and zinc, embedded in their bristles , although their long-term effectiveness is uncertain. Others have designed ionic toothbrushes that use electric currents to help loosen plaque , but they are dependent on batteries. Now, Yanhui Lu at Peking University in China and her colleagues have turned to studies showing that so-called piezoelectric materials fight bacteria in infected wounds and medical implants. These generate electric charges under pressure , prompting Lu’s team to develop toothbrush bristles made from piezoelectric plastic. science.title: Mars isn't dead — recent volcanic activity reveals it's just sleeping
science.description: null Scientists have long suspected that Mars is geologically "dead," but new spacecraft observations suggest the Red Planet's volcanoes are merely sleeping. That means that Olympus Mons , the extinct Martian volcano that at around 16 miles (26 kilometers) above the surrounding Martian plains is the largest mountain in the solar system , may in fact be a slumbering giant. The observations were made with the European Space Agency (ESA) mission ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter (TGO) as it studied volcanic fissures along the Alba Mons region of the Red Planet. Alba Mons is in the Tharsis region of Mars, the same area that is home to Olympus Mons. While the latter is the tallest volcano in the solar system, at 374 miles (600 km) across, about the size of Arizona, the Alba Mons region is the largest volcano when considering surface area. TGO detected gas containing hydrogen chloride making its way to the surface of Mars through the Alba Mons fissures. The same gas is commonly found escaping from magmatic vents on Earth, with the compound coming from hot magma beneath the surface. Detecting it on Mars is a sign of dormant Martian volcanism. Orbital imagery had previously shown some volcanoes appear to have been active within the last few million years, and seismometers have detected the rumbling of "marsquakes," both implying the Red Planet is volcanically active. However, eruptions and lava flows have been conspicuous by their absence. "Our findings suggest that Mars has retained enough internal heat to support volcanic activity until recently, and possibly still does," team co-leader and scientist at the Space Research Centre of the Polish Academy of Sciences, Daniel Mège, said in a statement sent to Space.com via email. "The TGO was able to find the smoking gun. It was like looking for a needle in a haystack." Evidence of dormant Martian volcanism is rising Mège and colleagues were first alerted to something strange happening on Mars when they noticed spikes of hydrogen chloride during Martian summer and on the northern hemisphere of the Red Planet. That is both a time and place at which hydrogen chloride shouldn't be detected. The gas usually peaks in the northern hemisphere during winter on Mars, disappearing in the summer. This variation is connected to the water and dust cycle on Mars. An exception to the rule occurs over volcanic fissures on the flanks of the Alba Mons volcano, in early summer. The TGO followed up on this by detecting fresh and narrow fissures, in some cases hundreds of feet long, in the Alba Mons region. A clear sign of volcanism. "It's truly amazing that it spotted a handful of molecules from a perhaps intermittent source, whilst moving continuously along its orbit to monitor the whole Martian atmosphere," Mège said.
